lessonRef.title: Launch and diagnostic: informal arguments for circumference, area, and volume formulas

sections.title: Instructional examples
sections.directions: Read the example first. You are not expected to know this yet.

items.prompt: Volume of a cone with radius 3 and height 4?

sections.title: Independent practice
sections.directions: Try each one. If you get stuck, write what you do know and move on.

items.prompt: Describe the cross-section formed by a cylinder cut by a plane perpendicular to its base through the axis.
A solid object has mass 21 g and volume 3 cm³. Find its density, and state whether it would float in water (density 1 g/cm³).
A square patio of side 3 m is to be paved at $6 per square metre. Find the total cost, and state which quantity the cost is proportional to.
choices: $18; the cost is proportional to the area
$72; the cost is proportional to the perimeter
$54; the cost is proportional to the area
$54; the cost is proportional to the side length

items.prompt: Find the volume of a square pyramid with base edge 7 and height 4. Leave π in the answer where it appears.
Describe the cross-section formed by a cylinder cut by a plane parallel to its base.

sections.title: Mastery check
sections.directions: Show what you can do so far. This sets the starting point, not a grade.
